Question: Shouldn't we refuse to vote this election seeing the 2 incompetent candidates we have to choose from?
Answer: Let me rephrase the question to be more transparent: Let Donald Trump win in 2024, please? I say that because it’s well established that the better the turnout in an election, the worse it goes for Republicans. Lots of people don’t vote. I get that, but I consider voting to be a civic duty for an American citizen. Look at the field and FIGURE IT OUT. And if you can’t figure it out, vote for Kamala Harris.

Question: Will AZ be forced to allow illegals to vote? https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/politics/republicans-ask-supreme-court-to-block-40-000-arizonans-from-voting-in-november/ar-AA1p2Ki9?ocid=mailsignout&pc=U591&cvid=5a6d642eb5c448c79d66c56a66c0f5fd&ei=111
Answer: The question is misleading. No one is saying that non-citizens (undocumented or legal permanent residents) can vote or should vote in Arizona. What Republicans in Arizona are doing is demanding that 40,000 registered voters who were not required to provide proof of citizenship when they registered, be summarily stricken from the voter rolls, whether they are citizens or not. So the better question is: Why do Republicans in Arizona want to kick 40,000 registered voters off the rolls with no evidence that they aren’t eligible? It’s not like the state couldn’t do a little research and figure it out who is who. The whole business is the result of a NEW LAW passed by Republicans in the Arizona Legislature, placing a requirement on voters who registered in years past when proof of citizenship was not required. Arizona Secretary of State Adrian Fontes said the appeal should be rejected. "There is no evidence of fraud and undocumented voting. The 2024 election is weeks away and acting now to restrict the voting rights of a large group of Arizona's voters is undemocratic," he said in a statement.[1] UPDATE: The Republican National Committee has sent a letter to 8 state secretaries of state, claiming that they are allowing non-citizens to vote. They said: … time and again, we have seen Democrat officials oppose basic safeguards and dismantle election integrity provisions, intentionally opening the door to non-citizen voting in our elections. And in proof of their case, they provided one single example of a non-citizen voter who claimed that he did not register to vote, but received a primary ballot in Minnesota by mail. No one has been able to verify the claim.

Name: Kevin Davidson
Question: People who think trolls ruined Quora: what new rules does this website need to stop them from disgracing it?
Answer: I don’t think we so much need new rules as we need the return of some old rules, specifically the ban on insincere questions. In times past Quora questions had to be open ended and expressed in neutral language. Now they can be political ads with a question mark on the end. The other change I would advocate is the ability to report profiles for repeated rule-violating content. Now we have to report EACH violation, which could run into the hundreds, rather than the profile. Clearly in the past couple years, the quality of discourse on Quora has circled the toilet and descended into the sewer. But I daresay, engagement is up.

Name: Kevin Davidson
Question: I have just had a comment deleted because it violated Quora's spam policy. It was a quote from The Washington Post with a link to Wikipedia. How can this be spam?
Answer: It’s probably not spam, but Quora filtering system is pretty simplistic. They look for the ratio of text to hyperlinks, and they look for the same link used in more than one comment. It has nothing to do with you, or the quality of your comment. Just appeal and they will restore it in less than a day, with a meaningless automated apology.
